summary: The weighted lattice centerpoint construction correctly applies Doignon's lattice Helly theorem to arbitrary positive real weights, places the selected lattice point in the convex hull of the positive-mass support, and uses convexity of the original body to prove that its fiber has positive mass. The affine selector is therefore defined at the selected point. The affine pullback of each boundary halfspace is handled correctly in both the proper-halfspace and degenerate full-space cases, the accepted boundary-reduction lemma applies without any zero-boundary-mass assumption, and summing the fiberwise depth bounds gives exactly beta times 2^{-n}. Positive-mass fibers are full-dimensional convex bodies, so their centroids are valid selectors and Grunbaum's inequality yields the stated centroid corollary with gamma_d.
